text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Croatian President Franjo Tudjman and his Bosnian counterpart Alija Izetbegovic are scheduled to meet after elections later in June.
- Government refuses request by the main opposition presidential candidate, recently injured at a rally, to postpone elections until July.
- First 20,000 Croatian refugees from Eastern Slavonia will return home by the autumn, a government official said.
- Social democrat and presidential candidate Zdravko Tomac said in a television interview his goal was to enter the second round of elections.
- The health food business in Zagreb is expanding and now boosts some 50 shops. Students and young people make up the majority of customers.
- Dalmatinska Banka which achieved 14.7 million kuna net profit in 1996 plans to increase it by 70 percent, it said in the annual report.
- Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka earned 219 million kuna in 1996 or 76 percent more than in the previous year, says chief executive Franjo Lukovic.
- Davor Stern, chief executive of oil concern INA says oil extracting should no longer only cover losses made by refineries, it has to make a profit and cover tax payments, which is not the case now.
- Prices of agricultural products grew faster than all other products in April, rising by 0.9 percent, state statistics show.
- The last mine in Croatia should close by 1998 by when some mines in Istria will be adapted for growing mushrooms.
- "I imagined the return to Vukovar differently," said opposition presidential candidate Vlado Gotovac in an interview, commenting on president Tudjman's recent visit.
